edges.effect_quant: Hibiscus shows a reproducible blood-pressure-lowering signal in randomized trials and pooled analyses. A 2022 meta-analysis covering 17 chronic trials and 1,018 adults found systolic blood pressure 7.10 mmHg lower than placebo or control, and a 2021 meta-analysis of 13 randomized trials with 1,205 participants found reductions in both systolic and diastolic pressure versus placebo.
edges.population: adults with elevated blood pressure or cardiometabolic risk, including women consuming hibiscus tea or Hibiscus sabdariffa preparations
edges.mechanism: Hibiscus polyphenols may improve endothelial function, provide mild diuretic and angiotensin-converting-enzyme-related effects, and reduce oxidative stress and inflammation. Those combined actions plausibly support modest blood pressure reduction.
edges.summary: The evidence leans clearly protective for blood pressure. Across randomized trials and meta-analyses, hibiscus preparations repeatedly reduce systolic pressure modestly, with somewhat smaller but still favorable diastolic effects.
edges.caveats: Most studies are short term, use varying hibiscus preparations, and are not limited to women-only samples. This edge should be interpreted as a modest adjunctive blood-pressure benefit rather than a substitute for established antihypertensive therapy in high-risk patients.

evidence.citation: Ellis LR et al 2022 Nutr Rev
evidence.notes: A systematic review and meta-analysis of the effects of Hibiscus sabdariffa on blood pressure and cardiometabolic markers.

effect_quant.comparator: systolic blood pressure with hibiscus versus placebo or control across chronic randomized trials
